fixed_transform_class.name: ARBITRARY_SHARED_UNIT_DISABLED_AUXILIARY_PADDING
definition: Start with CNF F={C_i} over original variables X.
Introduce any finite fresh auxiliary set Y.
For each original clause C_i choose an arbitrary subset Y_i of auxiliary literals, with each auxiliary y used only in one fixed polarity across padded clauses.
Replace C_i by P_i=C_i union Y_i.
For every auxiliary y that occurs in any padded clause, add one unit clause forcing y to the value that makes its padded literal false.
fixed_transform_class.nonlocality: The same auxiliary may appear in arbitrarily many padded clauses, so this includes global shared hubs and is strictly more nonlocal than private-per-clause padding.
fixed_transform_class.exactness: The forcing units make every added hub literal false; therefore the transformed CNF is logically equivalent to the original CNF after forgetting the fixed auxiliaries.

maxdef_conservation_theorem.statement: For every normalized CNF F, delta*(T_hub(F))=delta*(F).
proof: Take any selected transformed subformula Q. Let A be the selected padded original clauses and U the selected forcing-unit auxiliaries.
Let Y(A) be the set of fresh auxiliaries occurring in the selected padded clauses. Original and fresh variable sets are disjoint.
Thus deficiency(Q)=delta_F(A)+|U|-|Y(A) union U| <= delta_F(A) <= delta*(F), because |Y(A) union U|>=|U|.

For the reverse inequality choose an original sub-clause-set A0 attaining delta*(F), take its padded copies, and select exactly the forcing units for all auxiliaries in Y(A0). Then |U|=|Y(A0)| and Y(A0) union U=Y(A0), so deficiency equals delta_F(A0)=delta*(F).

R44BD_effect.meaning: Even a fresh auxiliary shared across arbitrarily many branches/clauses provides no maximum-deficiency credit when exactness is enforced merely by unit-fixing it to the disabling value.
R44BD_effect.selector_application: Adding shared unit-disabled hub literals to a raw selector merge cannot reduce the selector's additive maximum-deficiency debt.
R44BD_effect.strict_extension: R44BF private forced padding is the special case where each hub occurs in only one padded original clause. R44BI permits arbitrary sharing.

not_covered: auxiliaries constrained by non-unit shared functional relations
gadgets where auxiliary truth values depend nontrivially on original variables

next_admissible_math.question: Fix one shared auxiliary gadget with genuinely nontrivial functional constraints rather than unit disabling, then prove maxdef descent or an exact conservation/lower-bound theorem.
next_admissible_math.forbidden: Do not count another pattern of unit-forced shared padding as a new machine.
